title: Postgres 17 shipped a 4x faster VACUUM — here is our migration playbook
author: dbas_on_duty
snippet: We run 240 Postgres databases. VACUUM used to be our biggest maintenance window. This post covers the new memory tuning, what changed with the TID store, and the exact settings we rolled out: maintenance_work_mem, autovacuum_vacuum_cost_limit, and why our longest vacuum dropped from 6h to 47m.

title: Show HN: I built an AI-powered platform that revolutionizes content workflows
author: growth_hacker_9000
snippet: In today's fast-paced digital landscape, staying ahead of the curve is crucial. Our cutting-edge platform leverages the power of artificial intelligence to supercharge your content game. With seamless integrations and game-changing insights, the possibilities are endless. Sign up for early access today and unlock your team's true potential. Don't get left behind — the future of content is here.

title: You Won't Believe What This Developer Discovered Inside a 20-Year-Old Codebase
author: viral_dev
snippet: It started as an ordinary Tuesday. Then I opened the legacy repo. What I found next changed everything — and engineers at big tech companies are calling it 'the discovery of the decade.' Number 7 will shock you. I never could have predicted what was hiding in that git history, and when you see it, you'll understand why nobody is talking about it.

title: Writing a toy HTTP server in 200 lines of Rust with no dependencies
author: systems_sam
snippet: A walkthrough building a minimal HTTP/1.1 server on std::net::TcpListener only. Covers the request parser state machine, why we cap header size at 8KB, keep-alive handling, and the benchmark: 41k req/s on a laptop with zero crates. Full source in the post, 200 lines including comments.

title: 10 Game-Changing AI Tools Every Developer NEEDS in 2026
author: listicle_larry
snippet: Artificial Intelligence is transforming the way we work! In this article, we explore the top 10 must-have AI tools that will skyrocket your productivity. From code generation to smart assistants, these game-changing tools are essential in the modern developer's toolkit. Let's dive in!

title: SQLite as an application file format: two years in production
author: pragma_pat
snippet: We replaced our custom binary format with SQLite files for our desktop app. Post covers schema versioning inside the file, WAL vs delete journal for USB sticks, crash recovery stories (three real ones), and why we ship a VACUUM on every major upgrade. Includes measured file-size deltas versus our old format.

title: This One Database Trick Will Save You Hours of Work
author: seo_sally
snippet: Database developers everywhere are losing hours every single week. But there's a secret trick the pros don't want you to know. Once you learn it, you'll never look at your workflow the same way again. Read on to find out what it is!

title: Ask HN: Is anyone actually happy with their observability stack?
author: oncall_olive
snippet: Every vendor demo looks great until the bill arrives or the first big incident hits. We're on Datadog and the invoice is 5x what we budgeted. Curious what people actually like: Honeycomb, Grafana Cloud, self-hosted Prometheus + Tempo, or something else? What made you stay?

title: The electric car that thinks it's a phone: inside the dashboard OS wars
author: verge_staff
snippet: Automakers are shipping Android Automotive builds with app stores, subscriptions, and over-the-air updates. We drove three cars back to back and compared app latency, update cadence, and what happens when the LTE drops. One car wouldn't open its own glovebox without a cloud round-trip.

title: Why we deleted our microservices and went back to a modular monolith
author: mono_maya
snippet: Numbers first: deploys went from 45 min to 4, p99 went from 820ms to 190ms, infra bill down 60%. Post covers what actually hurt (distributed tracing of a 9-hop checkout, contract testing, 3 AM cross-service incidents), what we kept (separate data stores for two genuinely independent domains), and the strangler-fig plan we used over 7 months.

title: AI is the Future of Everything: Prepare Now or Be Left Behind
author: future_frank
snippet: The world is changing at lightning speed! Artificial Intelligence isn't just a buzzword — it's a revolution. In this post, we'll explore why AI matters, how it will change everything, and what you must do today to stay relevant. The time to act is now!

title: Debugging a kernel panic with only a serial cable and a print statement
author: bare_metal_ben
snippet: The appliance bricked in the field, no SSH, no console. This is the story of reproducing the panic on a bench unit, bisecting an upstream driver change, and the actual offending commit (a race in the DMA cleanup path). Includes the serial logging rig, ~$14 of parts, and the fix we upstreamed.

title: Launch: FluxCD 3.0 — gitops for the rest of us
author: flux_team
snippet: FluxCD 3.0 is out: single binary install, OCI artifacts by default, a real UI, and progressive delivery built in. Migration guide from 2.x included. Full changelog and benchmarks on 500-cluster fleets in the release notes.

title: Scientists Say This Common Habit Is Quietly Destroying Your Focus
author: viral_science
snippet: You do it every day. Everyone does. But according to a new study that nobody can seem to find, this common habit could be quietly destroying your ability to focus. The results will make you think twice. What is it? Keep reading.

title: A practical guide to Postgres row-level security with real policies
author: secu_rityfirst
snippet: Copy-paste-able RLS patterns that survive code review: tenant scoping with a membership join, why UPDATE policies need both USING and WITH CHECK, the auth.uid() default-column trick, and three test queries that prove each policy works. Every pattern is a runnable migration.

title: The hidden cost of serverless nobody mentions: cold starts at p50
author: latency_lisa
snippet: Everyone talks about p99 cold starts. Our problem was p50: our provider had degraded warm pools in one region for 6 weeks and nobody noticed because dashboards only alerted on p99. Data from 2.1M requests, the warm-pool metrics we now chart, and why we moved the checkout path back to containers.

title: Tell HN: I'm selling a course that will 10x your coding skills overnight
author: guru_gary
snippet: Most developers will never reach their full potential. But YOU can be different. My brand-new course reveals the secrets that separate 10x engineers from everyone else. Spots are limited and the price goes up soon. DM me for early bird access. Your future self will thank you!

title: I profiled 5 JSON parsers in Go. The winner surprised me.
author: bench_bob
snippet: Benchmarks on a 240MB NDJSON file: encoding/json, jsoniter, sonic, goccy, and bytedance's moon. Tables include allocs/op and GC pause impact, not just ns/op. The surprise: goccy wins on small docs but loses badly above 50MB due to a chunked-decode quirk. Repro script linked.

title: Everyone is wrong about the new laptop — a contrarian review
author: hot_take_hank
snippet: The internet has decided this laptop is bad. The internet is wrong. In this take, I explain why everyone else is missing the point, why the keyboard is actually fine, and why my experience is the only one that matters. Scroll to the end for my final verdict.

title: A catalog of every way we've broken production this year
author: blameless_brigade
snippet: 37 incidents, all written up. Common threads: config drift (11), unbounded queries (8), DNS (4), a build cache that silently reused stale artifacts (3), and one cat on a keyboard. Each entry has the trigger, detection time, and the guardrail we added. Detection time dropped from 41 min median to 9 after adding synthetic probes.

title: Unlock Your Potential: The Mindset Shift That Changed My Career Forever
author: mindset_mia
snippet: Success leaves clues! In this deeply personal post, I share the one mindset shift that transformed my career. It's not about talent — it's about how you think. Are you ready to unlock the best version of yourself? Let's go on this journey together!

title: Reverse-engineering a smart thermostat's proprietary protocol
author: packet_pete
snippet: The vendor cloud is being shut down, so 40,000 thermostats die in March. Post covers capturing frames with a $12 SPI sniffer, identifying the 16-bit CRC, and the full protocol doc now up on GitHub. Local control works; the firmware update mechanism is next.

title: 7 Habits of Highly Successful Programmers (Number 4 Will Shock You)
author: habit_hannah
snippet: What separates the best programmers from the rest? It's not what you think! These 7 powerful habits will transform the way you code forever. And when you get to number 4, you won't believe your eyes. Trust me on this one!

title: We open-sourced our internal design system: 60 components, Figma kit included
author: design_dana
snippet: Two years of internal work, MIT licensed. 60 accessible components (WCAG AA audited), theming via CSS variables, and a Figma kit that stays in sync via a token pipeline. Known gaps: no RTL yet, date picker is rough. Roadmap and contribution guide in the repo.

title: The Truth About 5G That Telecom Companies Don't Want You to Know
author: truth_teller
snippet: Billions have been spent on 5G. But what are they not telling you? The real story is more complicated than the ads suggest, and the details will surprise you. We investigated for months, and what we found changes everything.

title: TypeScript satisfies operator: 9 patterns we use daily
author: types_tina
snippet: Nine concrete patterns with before/after: config objects that keep literal types, exhaustive switches, zod-adjacent runtime validation, typed route tables. Each pattern lists the failure it prevents. No framework lock-in, plain tsc.

title: Ask HN: What did you learn maintaining someone else's code for a year?
author: inherit_ivan
snippet: I inherited a 400k-line codebase from a team that's gone. Curious what others learned from similar situations — what's worth investing in, what to leave alone, and the practices that actually paid off.

title: Local-first sync engine with CRDTs: what we got wrong in v1
author: sync_steve
snippet: Postmortem of our CRDT sync engine: GC of tombstones was O(n) and froze the app at 50k ops, we picked the wrong merge for ordered lists, and offline conflict UX confused everyone. v2 uses per-document lamport clocks and a rewritten list CRDT. Benchmarks for both versions included.

title: This Startup Says It Can End Traffic Jams Forever
author: pr_producer
snippet: Traffic jams cost the economy billions. But one bold startup says it has the answer. The founders are confident their technology will change cities forever. Skeptics aren't so sure. Here's what we know so far.

title: Understanding vector embeddings by building one from scratch
author: vector_vera
snippet: Build a 64-dimension embedding from co-occurrence counts in pure Python (no ML libraries), then compare its cosine similarities to a production model on the same corpus. Where the toy version holds up, where it collapses, and why. 80 lines of code total.

title: The DevOps Skills That Will Get You Fired (Avoid These!)
author: fear_fred
snippet: One wrong move and your career could be over! These DevOps mistakes have ended careers and destroyed teams. Make sure you're not doing number 3 — most engineers are! Protect yourself before it's too late.

title: eBPF in production: our journey from zero to packet filtering at the edge
author: kernel_kim
snippet: Concrete numbers: dropped abusive traffic at the NIC for 1/10th the CPU of iptables, load times for the filter program, and the verifier rejection that cost us two weeks. Includes our XDP program annotated line by line and the CI setup that tests it against a kernel matrix.

title: Why Nothing Matters Anymore (And That's Okay)
author: nihilist_nancy
snippet: Everything is noise now. Hot takes, endless feeds, breaking news about nothing. In this essay, I argue that caring less might be the answer. It's a perspective shift you didn't know you needed. Or maybe it isn't. Who's to say anymore?

title: Show DT: I made a CLI that turns cron expressions into plain English (and back)
author: cron_cathy
snippet: Ever been bitten by '*/5 2 * * 1-5'? This single-binary CLI parses cron into plain English and generates expressions from English. Handles 6-field and Quartz variants. 500 stars on day one, looking for edge-case bug reports — the Quartz day-of-week off-by-one is tracked in issue #4.

title: You Are Using Docker Wrong (Here's Why It Doesn't Matter)
author: container_carl
snippet: Everyone's doing it wrong, and honestly? It doesn't even matter. This provocative take will make you question everything you know about containers. But by the end, you'll realize the question was never about Docker at all.

title: Inside a CDN: we served 40Tbps on election night, here's the graph
author: edge_ops
snippet: Hour-by-hour traffic graphs, the three capacity decisions that mattered (pre-warming caches in swing-state metros, doubling anycast capacity for image assets, and moving the results page to streaming SSR), plus the one cache-invalidation bug that briefly showed 2020 numbers. Real numbers throughout.

title: The Ultimate Guide to Becoming a 10x Developer in 30 Days
author: ultimate_uma
snippet: Dream of becoming a 10x developer? This ultimate guide has everything you need! Follow these 30 days of life-changing tips and watch your productivity soar. Success is just one article away. Let's get started on this amazing journey!

title: How we cut our iOS app's launch time from 2.8s to 400ms
author: swift_sid
snippet: Methodical writeup: instrumentation first (os_signpost), then the wins ranked — dynamic framework linking (900ms), storyboards to code (400ms), redundant network gating at launch (600ms), image decoding on main thread (300ms). Includes the measurement harness and regression CI.

title: Is Web3 Dead? The Answer May Surprise You
author: chain_charlie
snippet: The bear market has been brutal. Many are asking if Web3 is dead. But the answer might not be what you expect! In this deep dive, we explore the question on everyone's mind. The truth is more nuanced than you think.

title: Our intern found a 12-year-old SQL injection. Here's the full timeline.
author: safe_sandra
snippet: Found via a fuzzing side project, not a breach — full disclosure process included. The vulnerable query was written in 2014 and survived 6 audits because it sat behind an admin-only route that marketing later exposed. Post covers the fix, the retro, and the parameterization lint rule we now run in CI.
